explanations.answer: The LORD and His holy words
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. He says he's like a drunkard "because of the LORD, because of His holy words." (Jeremiah 23:9) I think that tells you how heavy those words are to carry. His heart breaks and his bones tremble, and it all comes from taking God's word seriously.

Mockers don't come up anywhere in this verse, friend. The prophet says his heart is broken and his bones tremble "because of the LORD, because of His holy words." (Jeremiah 23:9) So what shakes him is what God has said. I know, a good heckler would be easier to blame.

Travel never comes up here. The prophet says he's like a man overcome by wine "because of the LORD, because of His holy words." (Jeremiah 23:9) His whole body is shaking, and the text says the cause is God's words. No suitcase involved.

Yes, ma'am, yes, sir. The prophet says the land is full of adulterers, "their course is evil and their power is misused." That's a heavy thing to hear. He's not hiding it, and I think that's why his heart is so broken.

The text says the opposite, friend. The prophet says of the people in the land, "their course is evil and their power is misused." So power is being misused, not used well. It's a heavy verse, and the prophet doesn't soften it.
Priest is right. The LORD says, "For both prophet and priest are ungodly." Both of them, together. The ones who spoke for Him and the ones who served in His house are named in the same breath.

House is right. The LORD says, "even in My house I have found their wickedness." Think about that. The place that belongs to Him is the very place He found it. I think that tells you how close to home this hits.

A king isn't named here, friend. The LORD says "both prophet and priest are ungodly." The ones He's calling out are the prophet and the priest. I know a king sounds like a big enough fish, but the text doesn't say it.

Field is a nice cookie-sheet-sized guess, but it's not in the verse. The LORD says He found their wickedness "even in My house." (Jeremiah 23:11) Not in a field, in His house. That's what makes it so serious.
No gate in this verse, baker. The LORD says, "even in My house I have found their wickedness." That's the place He names. And it's not a place where this should ever be found.

Right. The LORD says, "they will be driven away into the darkness and fall into it." The path is slick, they get pushed along it, and the darkness is where it ends. Not a spot I'd want to be, and I've spent time in the back of a dark drawer.

The wilderness does show up in this passage, but not here. In verse 10 the pastures of the wilderness have dried up. For the slick path, the LORD says they will be "driven away into the darkness and fall into it." That's the where.

Egypt isn't mentioned anywhere in these verses, friend. The LORD says their path will become slick and they will be "driven away into the darkness and fall into it." That's where the path leads. No passport needed.
True. The LORD says of the prophets of Samaria, "They prophesied by Baal and led My people Israel astray." They weren't just wandering off alone. They pulled His people along with them.
Not quite, friend. The LORD says of the prophets of Samaria, "They prophesied by Baal and led My people Israel astray." So they did lead His people astray. And the LORD calls it an offensive thing.
Yes. The LORD says, "They strengthen the hands of evildoers." Look who they're cheering on. The people who should be calling out wickedness are backing it up instead.
The poor aren't named in this verse, baker. The LORD says these prophets "strengthen the hands of evildoers." So the ones getting the boost are the wrong ones. It's a sad flip.

That sounds like a kind thing to do, doesn't it? But the LORD says something different: "They strengthen the hands of evildoers." The weary aren't named here. Their encouragement goes to the wrong crowd.

I see why you'd pick it, but the text says the opposite. The LORD says these prophets "strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns his back on wickedness." So people aren't turning away from it. They're staying right in it.

False, and you got it. The LORD says the prophets "strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns his back on wickedness." Nobody turns around, and I think that's the whole problem here. Their words keep people right where they are.
Sodom is right. The LORD says, "They are all like Sodom to Me; the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah." Two cities named together, and it's a heavy comparison. He doesn't say it lightly.

Babylon isn't the city in this verse, friend. The LORD says, "They are all like Sodom to Me; the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah." Sodom and Gomorrah go together in the same sentence. That's the pairing.

Nineveh isn't in this verse, baker. The LORD says, "They are all like Sodom to Me; the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah." The two cities named are Sodom and Gomorrah. That's the comparison He makes.

explanations.answer: Ungodliness spread from them through the land
explanations.explanation: That's the reason. The LORD says, "for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has spread throughout the land." It started with them and went everywhere. Wormwood and poisoned water are the heavy consequence He names for it.

explanations.answer: They moved their altars out to Samaria
explanations.explanation: Altars and moving trucks don't appear here. The LORD gives the reason Himself: "for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has spread throughout the land." It's about what spread from them. Samaria is mentioned a few verses earlier for something else.

explanations.answer: They stopped teaching the priests the law
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that, friend. The LORD says why He'll feed them wormwood: "for from the prophets of Jerusalem ungodliness has spread throughout the land." The reason is what spread from them. Teaching the law isn't mentioned.
It's the other way around, baker. The LORD of Hosts says, "Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you." That's a clear no. Don't listen to them.
False is right. The LORD of Hosts says, "Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you." He doesn't want the people hanging on those words. And He tells them why in the next lines.

That's it. The LORD says, "They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD." It's their own idea, not His word. Friend, it's like a recipe I made up and signed with somebody else's name.

explanations.answer: From the priests in the temple
explanations.explanation: Priests aren't named as the source here. The LORD says, "They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD." So the visions came from inside the prophets themselves. Not from anyone's mouth but their own.

explanations.answer: From the elders at the gate
explanations.explanation: Elders at a gate don't appear in this verse. The LORD says, "They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD." That's where these visions come from. Their own minds.

explanations.answer: No harm will come to you
explanations.explanation: Right. The LORD says they tell "everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart, 'No harm will come to you.'" That's the line. It sounds like comfort, but the LORD says these prophets are not speaking from Him.

explanations.answer: Turn back while you still can
explanations.explanation: That would be a warning, and these prophets aren't giving one. The LORD says they tell the stubborn, "No harm will come to you." Nothing about turning back. That's the message they keep repeating.

explanations.answer: The LORD has seen your sin
explanations.explanation: That's not what they say, friend. The LORD says they tell the stubborn, "No harm will come to you." They have nothing about sin to say at all. Just smooth, comfy words.
Storm is right. The LORD says, "the storm of the LORD has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down upon the heads of the wicked." It's moving already. That's serious weather.

Fire is not the word here, baker. The LORD says, "the storm of the LORD has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down upon the heads of the wicked." A storm, with a whirlwind inside it. Not a fire.

A plague is not in the verse, friend. The LORD says, "the storm of the LORD has gone out with fury, a whirlwind swirling down upon the heads of the wicked." It's a storm, and it's coming down on the wicked.
True. The LORD says, "The anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart." It doesn't turn around halfway. He finishes what He has set out to do.

Not this time, friend. The LORD says, "The anger of the LORD will not turn back until He has fully accomplished the purposes of His heart." So it keeps going until He's finished. The verse ends with, "In the days to come you will understand this clearly."
The LORD says no, friend. He says, "I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message." They ran on their own. He didn't send them.

False is right. The LORD says, "I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message; I did not speak to them, yet they have prophesied." They took off running without being sent. And He hadn't spoken to them either.

explanations.answer: Turned His people from their evil ways
explanations.explanation: Right. The LORD says, "if they had stood in My council, they would have proclaimed My words to My people and turned them back from their evil ways and deeds." Standing in His council is where the real message comes from. And that message turns people around.

explanations.answer: Gone off to prophesy in Samaria
explanations.explanation: Samaria isn't mentioned in this verse, baker. The LORD says if they had stood in His council, "they would have proclaimed My words to My people and turned them back from their evil ways and deeds." That's what they would have done. The prophets of Samaria came up earlier in a different spot.

Nothing about waiting years here, friend. The LORD says if they had stood in His council, "they would have proclaimed My words to My people and turned them back from their evil ways and deeds." They would have spoken His words. And the people would have turned back.
